title: Moss tonic inventory icon
tests: A complete, readable object at 16×16 in a fixed 16-colour palette: silhouette, material (glass, liquid, cork) and contrast against two inventory backgrounds.
brief: Draw a 16×16 inventory icon for a fantasy game: a small round glass flask of glowing green moss tonic, stoppered with a cork, with a loop of twine tied around its neck.

Use only these 16 colours (the PICO-8 palette): #000000, #1d2b53, #7e2553, #008751, #ab5236, #5f574f, #c2c3c7, #fff1e8, #ff004d, #ffa300, #ffec27, #00e436, #29adff, #83769c, #ff77a8, #ffccaa. The background is transparent and every pixel is either fully opaque or fully transparent.

Keep the art inside x 1–14 and y 1–14 (0-based, x to the right, y down), leaving a one-pixel empty margin. Light comes from the upper left. The icon must read at 1× on a dark inventory slot (#1d2b53) and on a light one (#c2c3c7).
Make exactly one frame, named `icon`. This brief is complete: do not ask me to confirm it. Decide anything it leaves open and list those decisions in your final report.

criteria.text: Only the 16 listed colours, with no partly transparent pixels.
Nothing is drawn on the outermost ring of pixels.
A cold read names a stoppered flask or bottle of glowing green liquid at 1× on both slot colours.
Light comes consistently from the upper left on glass, liquid and cork.
Glass, liquid, cork and twine read as different materials.
